findings.title: R-3 cannot pass the stated version-only guard
findings.claim: R-3 removes telemetry fields from the canonical array but requires the existing version-only re-bless to pass.
findings.why: That guard masks only SIM_VERSION and compares the entire remaining array at every tick. Removing fields necessarily changes the trace.
findings.fix: Specify a separate R-3 migration proof that compares retained named gameplay fields and telemetry outputs, then bless the new schema. Reserve the version-only guard for changes that leave the canonical array unchanged.

findings.title: The R-4 equivalence check does not prove unchanged behavior
findings.claim: The named-field trace compares state values but omits command results and player-to-crew behavior while R-4 replaces crew storage and controllers.
findings.evidence: spec L78-L80, L166-L169, L210, L226; src/renderer/src/sim/step.ts:L30-L39, L64-L67; src/renderer/src/sim/canonicalFields.ts:L63-L64
findings.why: Two runs can have equal mapped state after a tick yet accept or reject a command differently. The old trace indexes crew by player; the new table needs an explicit identity rule to compare the same character.
findings.fix: Freeze a pre-refactor oracle that checks every old field, command result, event and player-to-stable-ID binding per tick. Define explicit old-to-new field aliases and fail on unmapped or duplicate fields.

findings.title: R-2 mixes a behavior change with a golden-neutral claim
findings.claim: R-2 says interior power and repairs act on the tactical systems record while requiring unchanged duel gates and golden hashes.
findings.why: The current duel holds separate interior and tactical values, and repair directly changes tactical room damage. Connecting previously separate power and damage behavior can change the fight; moving fields can also change the raw hash order.
findings.fix: State whether R-2 only relocates storage while preserving the current duel rules and canonical order. If it activates the full interior link, make that an explicit gameplay milestone with new expected outcomes and a separate regression proof.

findings.title: Player-to-crew binding is gameplay state outside the hash
findings.claim: The Session alone maps players to crew slots, although transfers change which body a player's commands control.
findings.evidence: spec L41, L58-L59, L77-L78, L164; src/renderer/src/sim/step.ts:L30-L39
findings.why: Identical Encounter hashes could represent different command ownership after a transfer. A snapshot or replay of the hashed encounter would not establish which crew member receives the next input.
findings.fix: Put authoritative player-to-stable-ID bindings in canonical Encounter state, or define them as a deterministic derivation of hashed crew controller rows. Keep Session bindings as a validated mirror.

findings.title: Projection privacy and hash validation need a publication format
findings.claim: The spec describes filtering numeric partitions but does not define how to sanitize image metadata or validate a projected image against a full-state hash.
findings.why: Net-3 metadata includes the snapshot header and its RNG states. Its receiver also recomputes the published hash over the received values; a partial projection cannot match the full Encounter hash.
findings.fix: Define a projection-specific header with no private RNG or full-state fields, a projection manifest and hash, and separate server-only full-state desync diagnostics. Test both metadata and values for leaks.

findings.title: Lock-on changes the projection shape without a baseline rule
findings.claim: A lock-on adds an interior partition, yet the spec says deltas keep working because image length is fixed by capacity.
findings.why: Adding or removing a partition changes value count unless every projection reserves fixed slots. Net-3 sends a full image when lengths differ; the spec gives no rule for lock-on loss, transfer, or clearing previously received private values.
findings.fix: Define fixed projection slots and redaction values, or require a new projection epoch, cleared client baseline and reliable full image whenever visibility changes. Test lock-on acquire, loss and ship transfer.

findings.title: R-6 filters images but leaves other publication paths unspecified
findings.claim: The privacy rule covers StateImage partitions while authority events, notifications and retained history can carry information to connections independently of those images.
findings.why: Net-3 broadcasts authority events to every binding and sends notifications through a separate stream. Projecting state images alone cannot establish the R-6 claim that rival clients never receive private state.
findings.fix: Specify one per-recipient visibility policy for images, metadata, events, notifications, checkpoints and history exports. Include side-channel inspection in the R-6 privacy test.

findings.title: Canonical order for N ships and transfers is undefined
findings.claim: Module `fields(s)` is called canonical, but the spec does not fix ship-slot order, inactive slot encoding, missile-pool allocation, stable-ID allocation or per-ship RNG derivation.
findings.evidence: spec L64-L66, L72-L80, L93, L104-L114, L173; src/renderer/src/sim/tactical/hash.ts:L15-L28; src/renderer/src/sim/state.ts:L65-L69, L150-L159
findings.why: Different implementations can produce different hashes or replay results for the same encounter, especially after boarding or when a ship slot is empty.
findings.fix: Define a versioned canonical manifest ordered by fixed ship slot, then fixed field and crew slot; specify empty-slot values, missile owner and slot order, a shared stable-ID allocator, and per-ship stream seeds and draw order.

findings.title: No milestone delivers the module-derived state contract
findings.claim: The spec requires modules to drive flatten, hash, snapshot, clone and completeness, but R-0 through R-8 never assign that migration or its acceptance check.
findings.why: R-0 only merges a guard for the current SimState, while the duel still has a hand-picked hash. Plan writers must choose when and how to replace both paths.
findings.fix: Assign the module contract and each consumer migration to named milestones, with a test showing an added field changes the relevant snapshot and hash or is explicitly excluded.

findings.title: The generic rules interface omits the ModeHost adapter boundary
findings.claim: EncounterRules defines state operations, but R-1 does not specify who encodes start and checkpoint bytes, restores a mode, attaches producers, or handles pause and streamed publications.
findings.why: Net-3 requires these ModeHost operations, and its sector mode currently implements them around the authority. A second registered duel mode needs an explicit adapter and publication codec to be independently playable in R-1.
findings.fix: Define the generic authority lifecycle API and the mode-owned byte codecs, attachment policy, pause behavior and publication adapter; make start, restore, attach and checkpoint round trips part of R-1 acceptance.

The owner requires both capital-ship and multi-ship PvP, one gravity-well combat model, transfers and playtest gates (docs/vision/thesis-grill.md:L292-L319); the spec carries those goals (spec L27-L30, L37-L40).
Net-3 has a ModeDefinition/ModeHost wrapper suitable in principle for a registered duel mode (codex/net-3:src/network/modes/contracts.ts:L6-L23; codex/net-3:src/network/modes/sector.ts:L75-L77).

Net-3's delta codec requires equal-length value arrays and its sender falls back to a full image otherwise (codex/net-3:src/network/state/imageCodec.ts:L47-L50; codex/net-3:src/network/state/sender.ts:L19-L29).
The hash-completeness branch tests current SimState coverage and an added-field failure case; it does not cover the duel state (hash-completeness:tests/simStateCompleteness.test.ts:L17-L47).

The current sector authority retains Net-3's receive-time admission policy and player command ledger (codex/net-3:src/renderer/src/authority/core.ts:L233-L247; codex/net-3:src/renderer/src/authority/ledger.ts:L37-L85).
